70,wrong,"I took a trip to Thailand and was appalled at what I saw, from the filth and smut to the rampant corruption, prostitution, and hideous architecture. And through it all was the ever-present face of THE KING, hundreds of feet tall on skyscrapers, in subways, on office buildings, billboards...everywhere. Say anything critical of him and you're in big trouble.So my question going into this book was: How much is the King responsible for the Thailand that I experienced? For the innumerable narratives of abuse and extortion at the hands of government officials and one of the world's most deplorable legal systems?My answer after reading much of this book is that the King, even if not directly responsible for all that is foul in Thailand, is a huge power player in the utterly fragmented, rudderless, and byzantine world of this Southeast Asian power.
